Tomato___Bacterial_spot.recommendation: Avoid working with wet plants, reduce leaf wetness, and remove heavily infected plant material where appropriate. Consult local agricultural experts about approved management.

Tomato___Early_blight.recommendation: Remove heavily infected lower leaves, avoid overhead irrigation, rotate crops where possible, and seek advice on locally approved fungicides if disease pressure is significant.

Tomato___Late_blight.recommendation: Act promptly because the disease can spread rapidly. Avoid handling wet plants, isolate affected material where feasible, and contact an agricultural expert for confirmation and control advice.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.recommendation: Improve airflow, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and manage humidity. Seek local advice if the infection is spreading.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.recommendation: Remove infected lower leaves where practical, avoid overhead watering, and maintain good field sanitation. Seek advice about approved treatments.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.recommendation: Inspect the undersides of leaves for mites and webbing. Use integrated pest management and seek local advice before applying a miticide; avoid unnecessarily harming beneficial insects.

Tomato___Target_Spot.recommendation: Reduce leaf wetness, improve airflow, remove severely affected plant material where practical, and consult local experts about management.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.status: Possible tomato yellow leaf curl virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.recommendation: Inspect for whiteflies, which can spread the virus. Manage whiteflies using locally recommended integrated pest management. Remove severely affected plants where appropriate.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.recommendation: There is no curative treatment for infected plants. Sanitize tools, avoid handling plants after tobacco use, and seek advice on removing infected plants and preventing spread.

Tomato___healthy.recommendation: No disease-specific treatment indicated. Continue monitoring plants and maintain good irrigation and crop hygiene.

healthy_wheat.recommendation: No disease-specific treatment indicated. Continue crop monitoring and good field hygiene.

wheat_black_rust.recommendation: Inspect for dark rust pustules and seek local expert confirmation. Ask about locally approved management options.

wheat_blast.recommendation: Seek prompt confirmation from an agricultural specialist. Follow locally recommended disease-management measures.

wheat_brown_rust.recommendation: Inspect for reddish-brown pustules and seek local agricultural advice about severity and appropriate approved control measures.

wheat_fusarium_head_blight.recommendation: Inspect wheat heads and seek expert guidance. Grain quality and mycotoxin contamination may be concerns; do not assume affected grain is safe.

wheat_powdery_mildew.recommendation: Look for white powdery growth on leaves and stems. Consult an agricultural expert about management based on crop stage and disease severity.

wheat_smut.recommendation: Seek confirmation of the smut type. For future sowings, ask about certified seed and locally recommended seed treatments.

wheat_yellow_rust.recommendation: Inspect for yellow-orange pustules in stripes and seek prompt local agricultural advice about monitoring and approved control measures.

Bacterial Leaf Blight.recommendation: Use balanced fertilizer, avoid excessive nitrogen, maintain field sanitation, and consult local agricultural experts about resistant varieties and suitable management.

Brown Spot.recommendation: Check crop nutrition and water management. Use balanced fertilization and seek local advice about disease management and seed health.

Healthy Rice Leaf.recommendation: No disease-specific treatment indicated. Continue regular crop monitoring and appropriate field management.

Leaf Blast.recommendation: Avoid excessive nitrogen, monitor disease spread, and consult local agricultural experts about resistant varieties and approved control measures.

Leaf scald.recommendation: Inspect additional leaves and assess disease spread. Maintain field sanitation where practical and seek local expert guidance on management.

Sheath Blight.recommendation: Monitor affected sheaths, avoid excessive nitrogen, and consult local agricultural experts about suitable crop management and approved treatments.
